title: 1975 AHSME Problem 29
statement: What is the smallest integer larger than \((\sqrt3+\sqrt2)^6?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(\alpha=\sqrt3+\sqrt2\) and \(\beta=\sqrt3-\sqrt2.\) Adding their sixth powers cancels all odd radical terms: \[ \begin{aligned} \alpha^6+\beta^6 &=2\bigl(3^3+15(3^2)(2)\\ &\qquad+15(3)(2^2)+2^3\bigr)\\ &=970. \end{aligned} \] Since \(0\lt\beta\lt1,\) we have \(969\lt\alpha^6=970-\beta^6\lt970.\) Thus the smallest larger integer is \(970.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Pair the expression with its conjugate \((\sqrt3-\sqrt2)^6\)
Their sum is an integer, while the conjugate term lies strictly between \(0\) and \(1\)
